messages.content: Let's work on Sedona for Anil and me. We can do Thursday through Sunday, either November 4-7 or November 11-14. I want the comparison to include the real trip total, not just room rates: flights to Phoenix, rental car, three nights, resort charges, breakfast, and one spa treatment for each of us.

I can compare both weekends on that basis. Before I build the totals, should I use refundable hotel rates, and are nonstop SFO-PHX flights the right starting point? Also, do you want a compact rental car or something with more luggage room?

Use flexible hotel rates and nonstop flights. A midsize car is enough. We will each check one bag. Please look closely at the Phoenix arrival time because I do not want the drive to Sedona becoming unpleasant after a flight.

For November 4-7, the best-priced practical nonstop is 9:05 a.m.-11:03 a.m. outbound and 6:20 p.m.-8:25 p.m. return, at $596 for two including one checked bag each. A midsize rental is $286 including taxes. You should be out of the rental facility around noon and reach Sedona about 2:15-2:35 p.m., allowing for a brief stop.

For November 11-14, the lowest comparable nonstop is 12:15-2:13 p.m. outbound and 6:20-8:25 p.m. return, at $648 for two with bags. The car is $252. Rental-lot departure would likely be near 3:10 p.m., putting you in Sedona around 5:25-5:50 p.m. Sunset is about 5:25 p.m., so the last part of the drive would be at dusk or after dark.
That later arrival is not ideal. Is there an earlier flight on November 11 that does not make the airfare unreasonable?

Yes. There is a nonstop at 8:35-10:33 a.m. The total for two with checked bags is $712, or $64 more than the midday option. You would likely leave the rental facility around 11:30 a.m. and arrive at the resort around 1:45-2:05 p.m. The return remains 6:20-8:25 p.m.
Use that earlier flight when you price the second weekend. What are the resort choices?

Two properties fit the wellness focus. Canyon Light Resort has a flexible package that includes daily breakfast for two and a $300 spa credit. Its mandatory resort charge is separate. Red Rock Springs has a lower flexible room rate and much broader treatment availability, but breakfast, resort charges, and spa services are all additional. Both include self-parking in the resort charge.
Give me all four totals first. Keep the credits and fees visible so I can see what is driving the difference.

November 4-7 totals for two:

Canyon Light: airfare $596; rental $286; three flexible-rate nights with tax $2,394; resort charges $180; breakfasts $0; two treatments $520; spa credit minus $300; treatment service charges $104. Complete total: $3,780.

Red Rock Springs: airfare $596; rental $286; three flexible-rate nights with tax $1,848; resort charges $165; six breakfasts $240; two treatments $470; treatment service charges $94. Complete total: $3,699.

November 11-14, using the earlier outbound:

Canyon Light: airfare $712; rental $252; three nights with tax $2,466; resort charges $180; breakfasts $0; two treatments $520; spa credit minus $300; treatment service charges $104. Complete total: $3,934.

Red Rock Springs: airfare $712; rental $252; three nights with tax $1,782; resort charges $165; six breakfasts $240; two treatments $470; treatment service charges $94. Complete total: $3,715.
The second Red Rock total is only $16 more than the first weekend, despite the higher airfare. Is that correct?
Yes. The later weekend's room total is $66 lower and the rental is $34 lower, offsetting $100 of the $116 airfare increase. That leaves a net increase of $16: $3,715 versus $3,699.
Now check actual treatment availability. We would prefer Saturday, one treatment each, and they do not need to be simultaneous.

For November 6, Canyon Light has only one qualifying Saturday appointment, at 4:40 p.m.; the second treatment would have to be Friday at 2:30 p.m. or Sunday at 9:00 a.m. Red Rock Springs has Saturday openings at 10:20 a.m., 11:40 a.m., 1:10 p.m., and 3:00 p.m.

For November 13, Canyon Light can place one treatment at 11:30 a.m. and the other at 2:20 p.m. Red Rock Springs has multiple openings from 9:30 a.m. through 4:10 p.m., including adjacent 11:00 a.m. and 11:20 a.m. starts.
That makes the first weekend less attractive. Are the treatments comparable, or did you price different things?

They are comparable 60-minute customized massages. Canyon Light charges $260 per person before the package credit and service charge. Red Rock Springs charges $235 per person before service charge. The totals do not assume upgrades, add-ons, or extra gratuity beyond each spa's automatic 20 percent service charge.
What about cancellation terms for the later weekend? I want the room and spa exposure stated separately.

Canyon Light's room can be canceled without penalty through 6:00 p.m. Arizona time on October 28. After that, the penalty is the full three-night room-and-tax amount. Spa appointments can be canceled up to 24 hours before the first appointment; later cancellation is charged at the treatment price.

Red Rock Springs is refundable through 4:00 p.m. Arizona time on November 4. After that, the room penalty is one night plus tax, currently $594. Spa appointments have a 24-hour cancellation window and otherwise charge the full treatment price. Neither option is being held.
Let's narrow it to November 11-14. Before you give me the final two plans, is the return timing sensible with the drive back to Phoenix?

Yes. For the 6:20 p.m. departure, leaving Sedona at 1:30 p.m. provides about 2 hours 15 minutes for the drive and fuel, then roughly 25 minutes for the rental return and terminal transfer. That should put you at the terminal around 4:10 p.m., a little over two hours before departure. Even with 30 minutes of added road delay, the margin remains workable.
Good. Give me the two bookable plans for that weekend, including the tradeoff. Do not reserve anything yet.

Plan 1, Canyon Light package: November 11-14, three flexible-rate nights; nonstop flights 8:35-10:33 a.m. Thursday and 6:20-8:25 p.m. Sunday; midsize rental; breakfast for two each morning; one 60-minute massage each on Saturday at 11:30 a.m. and 2:20 p.m. Complete projected total is $3,934. This is the more integrated resort plan and the $300 spa credit is already applied, but it costs $219 more and has the stricter room cancellation penalty after October 28.

Plan 2, Red Rock Springs: the same flights and rental, three flexible-rate nights, breakfast budgeted at $40 per day for two, and Saturday massages at 11:00 a.m. and 11:20 a.m. Complete projected total is $3,715. It has broader appointment availability, a later no-penalty room deadline of November 4, and only a one-night room penalty afterward; breakfast and spa charges remain separate.

Both plans reach Sedona around 1:45-2:05 p.m. Thursday and use a 1:30 p.m. Sunday departure for Phoenix. Nothing has been booked or placed on hold.
